name: ACE-031
lead: ACE-031 is a soluble fusion protein of the activin receptor type IIB (ActRIIB) and the Fc part of IgG1. It acts as a decoy that binds myostatin and related ligands that limit muscle growth [1][2][5].

It was developed for muscle-wasting conditions and tested in healthy postmenopausal women and in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy [1][2][11]. The Duchenne trials were terminated [11]. It is not approved anywhere. Analytical chemists have published methods for detecting black-market ACE-031, indicating interest from athletes outside clinical settings [7][4].

paras: By binding myostatin (GDF-8) and other negative regulators, ACE-031 reduces their signalling through native receptors [2][5]. In mice, a 28-day treatment increased muscle mass independent of fibre type, unlike selective myostatin inhibition, which was reported to act mainly on type II fibres [3].

A single ascending-dose study in 48 healthy postmenopausal women (0.02-3 mg/kg subcutaneously versus placebo) found ACE-031 generally well tolerated, with injection-site reactions among reported adverse events [2]. A second phase 1 study in 70 healthy postmenopausal women was also registered [10].

A randomised, placebo-controlled ascending-dose trial in ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy had safety as its primary objective [1]. The phase 2 Duchenne study and its extension were terminated [11][12].
Preclinical work includes a 2025-2026 study reporting increased muscle mass and strength in common marmosets [6][8].

Anti-doping reviews list emerging muscle-regulating drugs such as ACE-031 as potential targets for misuse by athletes [4]. A 2025 paper described a gel-electrophoretic method for detecting black-market ACE-031 [7].

timeline.event: Phase 1 study in healthy postmenopausal volunteers begins [9].
Phase 2 Duchenne trial begins; later terminated [11].
Detection method for black-market ACE-031 published [7].

card.summary: An experimental myostatin-blocking fusion protein tested in healthy women and Duchenne boys; trials ended and it is not approved.

quick.overview:
ACE-031 is a lab-made decoy receptor designed to soak up myostatin and similar proteins that restrain muscle growth. It was tested for muscle-wasting disease.

It never reached approval, and anti-doping scientists have published detection methods for black-market versions.
quick.mechanism: It is a fusion of the activin receptor IIB with an antibody Fc piece. It binds myostatin and related ligands in the blood so they cannot signal in muscle.
quick.risks: The healthy-volunteer study reported it generally well tolerated, with injection-site reactions. The Duchenne trials were terminated, and it is unapproved.
